convert_binary_factors <- function(df) {
  # Find columns that are factors with exactly 2 levels
  binary_factor_cols <- names(df)[sapply(df, function(col) is.factor(col) && length(levels(col)) == 2)]
  
  for (col in binary_factor_cols) {
    first_level <- levels(df[[col]])[1]
    new_name <- paste0(col, ".", first_level)
    
    # 1 if first level, 0 if second level, preserving NA values
    df[[new_name]] <- ifelse(is.na(df[[col]]), NA_real_, ifelse(df[[col]] == first_level, 1, 0))
    
    # Remove original column
    df[[col]] <- NULL
  }
  
  return(df)
}

library(dplyr)

sample_n_students <- function(df, N, 
                              school_col = "school_id", 
                              student_col = "student_id", 
                              year_col = "year") {
  
  if (N > nrow(df)) {
    stop(paste("Requested N (", N, ") is larger than total available rows (", nrow(df), ")."))
  }
  
  # 1. Get unique observations (student-school-year combinations)
  obs_df <- df |> 
    distinct(across(all_of(c(school_col, student_col, year_col))))
  
  if (N > nrow(obs_df)) {
    stop(paste("Requested N (", N, ") is larger than unique student-school-year records (", nrow(obs_df), ")."))
  }
  
  # 2. Shuffle randomly upfront
  obs_shuffled <- obs_df[sample(nrow(obs_df)), ]
  
  # 3. Interleave by year AND school so selection cycles evenly across all years and schools
  selected_obs <- obs_shuffled |> 
    group_by(across(all_of(c(year_col, school_col)))) |> 
    mutate(rank_within_group = row_number()) |> 
    ungroup() |> 
    # Sorting by rank interleave-samples evenly across combinations
    arrange(rank_within_group) |> 
    slice_head(n = N)
  
  # 4. Filter original dataset
  df |> 
    inner_join(
      selected_obs |> select(all_of(c(school_col, student_col, year_col))), 
      by = c(school_col, student_col, year_col)
    )
}

decorated_dt <- function(data, digits = 3) {
  num_cols <- which(sapply(data, is.numeric))
  names(num_cols) <- NULL
  
  datatable(data, 
            options = list(
              scrollX = TRUE,
              columnDefs = 
                list(list(targets = num_cols,  # JS uses 0-based indexing
                     render = JS(sprintf(
                       "function(data, type, row){ 
                          if (data === null || isNaN(data)) { return 'NA'; }
                          return data.toFixed(%d); 
                        }", digits
                     ))))
              
            ))
}

plot_boxplots <- function(data, cont_var) {
  # Find discrete (non-numeric) columns, excluding the continuous one
  disc_vars <- names(data)[sapply(data, is.factor)]
  disc_vars <- setdiff(disc_vars, cont_var)
  
  # Build a plot for each discrete variable
  plots <- lapply(disc_vars, function(var) {
      plot_data <- data[!is.na(data[[cont_var]]) & !is.na(data[[var]]), ]
    ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = .data[[var]], y = .data[[cont_var]])) +
      geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
      labs(x = var, y = cont_var,
           title = paste(cont_var, "by", var)) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  })
  
  # Arrange all plots
  plots
}

# Регрессия без регуляризации

```{r eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
set.seed(42)
pisa |> filter(country == "FRA") |> select(-dishwasher) |> group_by(year) |> summarise(total = n(), complete = sum(complete.cases(pick(everything()))))
visualise_data <- pisa.log |> select(-dishwasher) |> filter(country == "FRA", father_educ > "ISCED 1", mother_educ > "ISCED 1") |> filter(complete.cases(pick(everything()))) |> sample_n_students(2000)
ggpairs(visualise_data |> select(math, read, science, year, escs, wealth, gender, mother_educ),
       lower = list(continuous = "points", combo  = "points"), 
       upper = list(continuous = wrap("points")),       
       diag = list(continuous = wrap("barDiag")))
```

```{r}
plot_boxplots(visualise_data, "read")
```

```{r}
pisa.log.regr <- pisa.log |> select(-dishwasher, -stu_wgt.log) |>
    filter(country == "FRA", father_educ > "ISCED 1", mother_educ > "ISCED 1") |>
    filter(complete.cases(pick(everything()))) |>
    mutate(year = as.integer(year),
           television = as.integer(television),
           computer_n = as.integer(computer_n),
           car = as.integer(car),
           book = as.integer(book),
           mother_educ = factor(mother_educ, ordered=F),
           father_educ = factor(father_educ, ordered=F))
set.seed(42)
idx <- sample(nrow(pisa.log.regr), 0.7 * nrow(pisa.log.regr))
pisa.log.train <- pisa.log.regr[idx, ]
pisa.log.test  <- pisa.log.regr[-idx, ]
```

```{r}
model.full <- lm(read ~ .,
                 pisa.log.train |> select(-country, - school_id, - student_id)) # , -math, -science
model.full |> lm.beta() |> summary()
```

```{r}
# backward даёт year + father_educ + gender + computer + internet + math + science + desk + car + book + wealth + escs

step.backward <- stepAIC(model.full, scope=list(upper = ~ ., lower = ~1), 
                    trace=F, direction="backward")
step.backward |> lm.beta() |> summary()

cor(pisa.log.test$read, predict(step.backward, pisa.log.test))^2
```

## попробуем не брать math и science

```{r}
model.full <- lm(read ~ .,
                 pisa.log.train |> select(-country, - school_id, - student_id, -math, -science))
model.full |> lm.beta() |> summary()
```

```{r}
# backward даёт year + gender + internet + math + science + computer_n + book + wealth
step.backward <- stepAIC(model.full, scope=list(upper = ~ ., lower = ~1), 
                    trace=T, direction="backward")
step.backward |> lm.beta() |> summary()

cor(pisa.log.test$read, predict(step.backward, pisa.log.test))^2
```

# Регрессия с регуляризацией

## $L^2$-регуляризация

```{r}
y <- pisa.log.train |> na.omit() |> model.matrix(~ read - 1, data=_) |> scale(center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
X <- pisa.log.train |> na.omit() |> model.matrix(~ . -country -student_id -school_id -read - 1, data=_) 
```
```{r}
# Perform 10-fold cross-validation to select lambda ---------------------------
lambdas_to_try <- 10^seq(-3, 1, length.out = 150)
# Setting alpha = 0 implements ridge regression
ridge_cv <- cv.glmnet(X, y, alpha = 0, lambda = lambdas_to_try,
                      standardize = TRUE, nfolds = 20)
# Plot cross-validation results
plot(ridge_cv)

lambda_cv <- ridge_cv$lambda.min
lambda_cv
# Fit final model, get its sum of squared residuals and multiple R-squared
model_ridge_cv <- glmnet(X, y, alpha = 0, lambda = lambda_cv, standardize = TRUE)

cor(pisa.log.test$read, predict(model_ridge_cv, pisa.log.test|> model.matrix(~ . -country -student_id -school_id -read - 1, data=_) ))^2
```

```{r}
res <- glmnet(X, y, alpha = 0, lambda = lambdas_to_try, standardize = FALSE)
plot(res, xvar = "lambda")
legend("bottomright", lwd = 1, col = 1:29, legend = colnames(X), cex = .7)
```

## $L^1$-регуляризация (LASSO)

```{r}
# Perform 10-fold cross-validation to select lambda ---------------------------
#lambdas_to_try <- 10^seq(-3, 5, length.out = 100)
# Setting alpha = 1 implements lasso regression
lasso_cv <- cv.glmnet(X, y, alpha = 1, lambda = lambdas_to_try,
                      standardize = TRUE, nfolds = 10)
# Plot cross-validation results
plot(lasso_cv)

lambda_cv_min <- lasso_cv$lambda.min
lambda_cv_1se <- lasso_cv$lambda.1se
# Fit final model, get its sum of squared residuals and multiple R-squared
model_cv_lasso <- glmnet(X, y, alpha = 1, lambda = lambda_cv_min, standardize = TRUE)
model_cv_lasso |> coef()

cor(pisa.log.test$read, predict(model_cv_lasso, pisa.log.test|> model.matrix(~ . -country -student_id -school_id -read - 1, data=_) ))^2

model_cv_lasso <- glmnet(X, y, alpha = 1, lambda = lambda_cv_1se, standardize = TRUE)
model_cv_lasso |> coef()

cor(pisa.log.test$read, predict(model_cv_lasso, pisa.log.test|> model.matrix(~ . -country -student_id -school_id -read - 1, data=_) ))^2
```
Итого отбор признаков в обычной регрессии:

year + gender + internet + math + science + computer_n + book + wealth

(0.7302)

Отбор при помощи LASSO:

year + mother_educ + gender + internet + math + science + computer_n + car + book

(0.7293)
